notes: Company background: YC S21 spinout building a GitHub-integrated PR assistant used by mid-size engineering teams; product surfaces inline suggestions, bulk comment generation and PR summaries.
Primary ask: low-latency streaming for IDE copilots + high-quality PR comment generation. Must support model/version pinning per-customer and deterministic reranker for comment ordering.
Workload profile: many small PRs (avg 12 changed lines), occasional large refactors. Baseline target: 300 sustained RPS for small diffs, burst to 2k RPS during release windows.
Latency SLOs: first token < 50ms for streaming in-editor experience; 95th < 150ms for short summary endpoints; end-to-end comment generation for 20-line diff < 700ms.
Quality metrics of interest: precision/recall on suggested comments, false-positive rate (no incorrect code edits), human edit rate after suggest, reranker NDCG vs current heuristic.
Model preferences: prefer open weights (LLMs) they can pin; want quantized options for cost. Must be able to pin model version by commit-sha and fall back to smaller variant under capacity pressure.
Caching/efficiency ask: prefix + KV cache support, per-repo prefix caching, advice on batching config to balance token-cost vs latency; desire for automatic cache warmups for common codebases.
Security/compliance: SOC2 required, SAML SSO for enterprise customers, audit logs for every inference, KMS integration for key management, ability to redact PII from logs on demand.
Data residency: majority NA but top-5 customers require EU residency; blocker until Redwood confirms region options for dedicated/private deployments.

POC plan: 2-week dedicated pool POC. Deliverables: perf dashboard (latency, token breakdown), quality evaluation on 500 PRs (precision/recall), cost per review estimate, security questionnaire answers.
Integration details: GitHub App webhook + restful batch endpoints; webhooks for comment placement, optional streaming websocket for IDE; requirement for idempotent request semantics.
Engineering quote: "we need streaming in-editor — if the user opens a file we should start incremental summary; waiting for >200ms kills UX" (Eng Lead).
CTO quote: "determinism and low hallucination is non-negotiable — suggestions must not propose incorrect API usage" — heavy on regression testing and eval sets.
Decision criteria: model quality first, then predictable cost and enterprise security. If Redwood meets perf + security, they prefer Redwood over building an internal serving layer.
Commercial constraints: willing to commit to reserved capacity for predictable latency; target ARR band $50k-$150k depending on included private tenant options and observability retention.
Open technical questions: how Redwood handles model rollbacks mid-POC, KV cache eviction semantics across repos, tokenized cost estimates for structured comment generation (function-calling output).
Legal blockers: negotiation around inference data retention and right-to-delete; asked for example contract language for PII deletion and audit support.
Next tactical steps: SE to deliver POC configuration (GPU sizing + pool sizing) by 2026-03-05; security to respond to SEC-4420 ticket with log retention options and KMS flows.
